boundary_note: Bounded first pass for both frozen records in Forrest's Expedition into West Tennessee. Preserve per-engagement dates: Jackson December 19 and Parker's Cross Roads December 31, 1862. Lexington, Trenton, Humboldt and other actions of the expedition are not added. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force text names two regiments of the Jackson garrison and a detachment of Forrest's cavalry of approx. 400, with structured Confederate bounds of 400/400; the live field reads zero. NPS gives Forrest's whole brigade as 2,100 men; Jordan and Pryor give about 1,800 officers and men and four guns at the outset.
claims.rationale: Detachment, brigade and outset figures are different populations; the brigade figures differ between the sources. None is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: NPS says Sullivan ordered Englemann out with a small force, and names Englemann's two infantry regiments. The live heading ranks Forrest Major General against the frozen Brigadier General, which the NPS narrative also uses.
claims.rationale: Garrison and field command are distinct; neither listed commander receives automatic sole credit. The heading rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen result is Confederate victory, as is the live field. NPS says Englemann's regiments repulsed a Confederate mounted attack and that the Federals checked a demonstration while other Confederates fulfilled part of the mission; Jordan and Pryor say the Federals were driven to their entrenchments.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The sources describe the local fight differently; the frozen label is retained.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Total unknown (US 6; CS unknown); the live NPS field reads 6 total (US 6; CS 0;). Jordan and Pryor claim a Federal loss of about thirty killed and wounded in the December 19 skirmish, and about five hundred prisoners from the several combats around Jackson.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The live CS zero replaces a frozen 'unknown' and is not measured absence; the prisoner figure spans several actions.

open_questions: Englemann's and Forrest's reports, returns and the division of losses among the actions around Jackson remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family; Jordan and Pryor is one retrospective Confederate history written from Forrest's papers and notes, for most of whose statements Forrest's prefatory note accepts responsibility. It is not independent of the listed Confederate commander. Reports and newspapers quoted inside it are not additional families.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
